sources.entry: Hister - Personal web search engine with automatic indexing of visited websites. Supports offline local result previews, local files, multi-user handling and optional semantic search. (Demo, Source Code) AGPL-3.0 Go/Docker

summary.one_liner: Nogon (formerly Hister) is a self-hosted personal search engine that full-text indexes the web pages you visit and the local files you keep.
summary.what_it_does: Nogon runs a local or self-hosted server that indexes the full contents of pages you visit (via a Firefox or Chrome browser extension) and of local files and directories you choose. Pages can also be added by a crawler, and existing browser history and bookmarks can be imported. Search is available from the web interface, a terminal UI, the command line, and an AI assistant connected through MCP. Queries support field filters, phrases, wildcards, negation, aliases, and result priorities. An optional semantic search mode finds documents by meaning using an embeddings endpoint the user configures. Multiple users can share one server with their documents and results kept separate.
use_cases: find a web page I visited earlier
search my browser history and bookmarks
index and search local files and folders
private personal search on my own server
give an AI assistant access to my saved documents
share a search index among several users
how_to_run: Download the binary for your platform from the latest release and rename it to nogon (nogon.exe on Windows)
On Linux or macOS: chmod +x nogon
Start the server: ./nogon listen (on Windows: .\nogon.exe listen in PowerShell)
Install the browser extension for Firefox or Chrome
Visit a page with the extension enabled, then search Nogon for a phrase from that page
notable: Indexes full page contents and local files, not just titles and URLs
Exposes search through an MCP interface for AI assistants
Optional semantic search through a user-configured embeddings endpoint
No telemetry or mandatory cloud service; runs on infrastructure you control
caveats: Server must be kept running in a terminal for pages to be indexed and searched
Semantic search sends document text to the embeddings endpoint you choose
Building from source requires Go 1.26, npm, and a C compiler
